# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

```text
Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)
  -a, --dryness                            calculate the DRYness of the project (implies --uloc)
      --eaf float                          the effort adjustment factor derived from the cost drivers (1.0 if rated nominal) (default 1)
      --exclude-dir strings                directories to exclude (default [.git,.hg,.svn])
  -x, --exclude-ext strings                ignore file extensions (overrides include-ext) [comma separated list: e.g. go,java,js]
  -n, --exclude-file strings               ignore files with matching names (default [package-lock.json,Cargo.lock,yarn.lock,pubspec.lock,Podfile.lock,pnpm-lock.yaml])
      --file-gc-count int                  number of files to parse before turning the GC on (default 10000)
      --file-list-queue-size int           the size of the queue of files found and ready to be read into memory (default 8)
      --file-process-job-workers int       number of goroutine workers that process files collecting stats (default 8)
      --file-summary-job-queue-size int    the size of the queue used to hold processed file statistics before formatting (default 8)
  -f, --format string                      set output format [tabular, wide

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Example badge URL:
```
https://sloc.xyz/github/boyter/scc/
```

Note that you don't have to specify the directory you want to run against. Running `scc` will assume you want to run against the current directory.

You can also run against multiple files or directories `scc directory1 directory2 file1 file2` with the results aggregated in the output.

## Features

`scc` includes many features to help you count code accurately:

- Very fast and gets faster the more CPU you throw at it
- Accurate
- Works very well across multiple platforms without slowdown (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Large language support
- Can ignore duplicate files
- Has complexity estimations
- You need to tell the difference between Coq and Verilog in the same directory
- cloc yaml output support so potentially a drop in replacement for some users
- Can identify or ignore minified files
- Able to identify many #! files
- Can ignore large files by lines or bytes
- Can calculate the ULOC or unique lines of code by file, language or project
- Supports multiple output formats for integration, CSV, SQL, JSON, HTML and more

## Complexity Estimates

Complexity estimates are provided for supported languages. The complexity estimate is an approximation similar to cyclomatic complexity. The intent is not to be perfect but provide a good enough indication of complexity.

Example output with complexity enabled:

```text
$ scc --complexity
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076
```

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
</output>

Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.
Version 3.7.0
Ben Boyter <ben@boyter.org> + Contributors

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --cost-comparison                    show both COCOMO and LOCOMO estimates side by side
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)
  -a, --dryness                            calculate the DRYness of the project (implies --uloc)
      --eaf float                          the effort adjustment factor derived from the cost drivers (1.0 if rated nominal) (default 1)
      --exclude-dir strings                directories to exclude (default [.git,.hg,.svn])
  -x, --exclude-ext strings                ignore file extensions (overrides include-ext) [comma separated list: e.g. go,java,js]
  -n, --exclude-file strings               ignore files with matching names (default [package-lock.json,Cargo.lock,yarn.lock,pubspec.lock,Podfile.lock,pnpm-lock.yaml])
      --file-gc-count int                  number of files to parse before turning the GC on (default 10000)
      --file-list-queue-size int           the size of the queue of files found and ready to be read into memory (default 96)
      --file-process-job-workers int       number of goroutine workers that process files collecting stats (default 96)
      --file-summary-job-queue-size int    the size of the queue used to hold processed file statistics before formatting (default 96)
  -f, --format string                      set output format [tabular, wide, json, json2, csv, csv-stream, cloc-yaml, html, html-table, sql, sql-insert, openmetrics] (default "tabular")
      --format-multi string                have multiple format output overriding --format [e.g. tabular:stdout,csv:file.csv,json:file.json]
      --gen                                identify generated files
      --generated-markers strings          string markers in head of generated files (default [do not edit,<auto-generated />])
  -h, --help                               help for scc
  -i, --include-ext strings                limit to file extensions [comma separated list: e.g. go,java,js]
      --include-symlinks                   if set will count symlink files
  -l, --languages                          print supported languages and extensions
      --large-byte-count int               number of bytes a file can contain before being removed from output (default 1000000)
      --large-line-count int               number of lines a file can contain before being removed from output (default 40000)
      --locomo                             enable LOCOMO (LLM Output COst MOdel) cost estimation
      --locomo-config string               LOCOMO power-user config "tokensPerLine,inputPerLine,complexityWeight,iterations,iterationWeight"
      --locomo-cycles float                override estimated LLM iteration cycles (default: calculated from complexity)
      --locomo-input-price float           LOCOMO cost per 1M input tokens in dollars (overrides preset)
      --locomo-output-price float          LOCOMO cost per 1M output tokens in dollars (overrides preset)
      --locomo-preset string               LOCOMO model preset [large, medium, small, local] (default "medium")
      --locomo-review float                human review minutes per line of code for LOCOMO estimate (default 0.01)
      --locomo-tps float                   LOCOMO output tokens per second (overrides preset)
      --mcp                                start as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over stdio
      --min                                identify minified files
  -z, --min-gen                            identify minified or generated files
      --min-gen-line-length int            number of bytes per average line for file to be considered minified or generated (default 255)
      --no-cocomo                          remove COCOMO calculation output
  -c, --no-complexity                      skip calculation of code complexity
  -d, --no-duplicates                      remove duplicate files from stats and output
      --no-gen                             ignore generated files in output (implies --gen)
      --no-gitignore                       disables .gitignore file logic
      --no-gitmodule                       disables .gitmodules file logic
      --no-hborder                         remove horizontal borders between sections
      --no-ignore                          disables .ignore file logic
      --no-large                           ignore files over certain byte and line size set by large-line-count and large-byte-count
      --no-min                             ignore minified files in output (implies --min)
      --no-min-gen                         ignore minified or generated files in output (implies --min-gen)
      --no-scc-ignore                      disables .sccignore file logic
      --no-size                            remove size calculation output
  -M, --not-match stringArray              ignore files and directories matching regular expression
  -o, --output string                      output filename (default stdout)
      --overhead float                     set the overhead multiplier for corporate overhead (facilities, equipment, accounting, etc.) (default 2.4)
  -p, --percent                            include percentage values in output
      --remap-all string                   inspect every file and remap by checking for a string and remapping the language [e.g. "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header"]
      --remap-unknown string               inspect files of unknown type and remap by checking for a string and remapping the language [e.g. "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header"]
      --size-unit string                   set size unit [si, binary, mixed, xkcd-kb, xkcd-kelly, xkcd-imaginary, xkcd-intel, xkcd-drive, xkcd-bakers] (default "si")
      --sloccount-format                   print a more SLOCCount like COCOMO calculation
  -s, --sort string                        column to sort by [files, name, lines, blanks, code, comments, complexity] (default "files")
      --sql-project string                 use supplied name as the project identifier for the current run. Only valid with the --format sql or sql-insert option
  -t, --trace                              enable trace output (not recommended when processing multiple files)
  -u, --uloc                               calculate the number of unique lines of code (ULOC) for the project
  -v, --verbose                            verbose output
      --version                            version for scc
  -w, --wide                               wider output with additional statistics (implies --complexity)
EOF
cat /tmp/help_capture.txt

./executable --help 2>&1 | diff -u /tmp/help_capture.txt - && echo "help matches" || echo "help diff above"
"}

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. def get(code_lines, comp):
    # generate code with code_lines code and comp complexity as before
    if comp==0:
        lines=["def f():"]
        for i in range(code_lines-1):
            lines.append(f"    x{i}=1")
        code="\n".join(lines)+"\n"
    else:
        snippet=" and ".join([f"a{i}" for i in range(comp+1)])
        lines=["def f():", f"    x = {snippet}"]
        for i in range(code_lines-2):
            lines.append(f"    y{i}=1")
        code="\n".join(lines)+"\n"
    path="/tmp/fit.py"
    open(path,"w").write(code)
    out=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["./executable",path,"--locomo","--format","json2"], text=True))
    summ=out['languageSummary'][0]
    inp=out['estimatedLLMInputTokens']
    outp=out['estimatedLLMOutputTokens']
    avg=out['estimatedLLMAverageComplexityMultiplier']
    cyc=out['estimatedLLMCycles']
    return summ['Code'], summ['Complexity'], inp, outp, avg, cyc

points=[]
for cl in [6,10,20,30]:
    for comp in [0,1,2,4,8]:
        cc, co, inp, outp, avg, cyc = get(cl, comp)
        points.append((cc, co, inp, outp))
        print(f"cl {cl} comp {comp} -> code{cc} comp{co} inp{inp:.1f} out{outp:.1f} avg{avg:.3f} cyc{cyc:.3f}")

# Try fit input = a*code + b*comp + c*sqrt(code*comp)
import numpy as np
# Build matrix
A=[]
b=[]
for code, comp, inp, outp in points:
    A.append([code, comp, math.sqrt(code*comp) if comp>0 else 0])
    b.append(inp)
A=np.array(A)
b=np.array(b)
# Solve least squares
coeff, residuals, rank, s = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)
print("coeff input a,b,c", coeff, "residual", residuals)
# Predict
for (code, comp, inp, outp), row in zip(points, A):
    pred = coeff[0]*code + coeff[1]*comp + coeff[2]*math.sqrt(code*comp) if comp>0 else coeff[0]*code
    print(f"code {code} comp {comp} inp {inp:.1f} pred {pred:.1f} err {inp-pred:.1f}")

print("--- fit output similarly ---")
A2=[]
b2=[]
for code, comp, inp, outp in points:
    A2.append([code, comp, math.sqrt(code*comp) if comp>0 else 0])
    b2.append(outp)
A2=np.array(A2)
b2=np.array(b2)
coeff2, _,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(A2,b2, rcond=None)
print("coeff out", coeff2)
for (code, comp, inp, outp) in points:
    pred = coeff2[0]*code + coeff2[1]*comp + coeff2[2]*math.sqrt(code*comp) if comp>0 else coeff2[0]*code
    print(f"code {code} comp {comp} out {outp:.1f} pred {pred:.1f} err {outp-pred:.1f}")

# Try alternative model: input = code*30 * (1 + cw*sqrt(comp/code))
# Fit cw
# Compute cw per point as (inp/(30*code)-1)/sqrt(comp/code)
print("--- cw per point input ---")
for code, comp, inp, outp in points:
    if comp==0: continue
    base=30*code
    cw=(inp/base -1)/math.sqrt(comp/code)
    print(f"code {code} comp {comp} cw {cw:.3f}")

    # Simple heuristic: if contains NUL -> binary unless flag disabled
    # Use naive: if b'\x00' in data => binary
    # To more closely match observed, we'll use threshold: if b'\x00' in data[:8000] then binary if count >1 or not at end?

    if b'\x00' in data:

# Minified / generated detection
def is_minified(bytes_len, lines, threshold=255):
    if lines == 0:
        return False
    avg = bytes_len / lines
    return avg > threshold

def is_generated(content, markers=None):
    if markers is None:
        markers = ["do not edit","<auto-generated />"]
    # Check first 1024 bytes head for markers case-insensitive
    head = content[:2048].decode(errors='ignore').lower()
    for m in markers:
        if m.lower() in head:
            return True
    return False

# Helper to parse count-as string
def parse_count_as(s):
    # format: "jsp:htm,chead:\"C Header\" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header"
    # s is like "jsp:htm" or "jsp:htm,chead:\"C Header\""
    # Need to handle quotes
    result={}
    if not s:
        return result
    # Use csv-like split respecting quotes? Simplify split by comma not inside quotes
    parts=[]
    cur=""
    in_quote=False
    quote_char=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_quote:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==quote_char:
                in_quote=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_quote=True
                quote_char=ch
                cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip())
                cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        if ":" not in p:
            continue
        k,v = p.split(":",1)
        k=k.strip()
        v=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        # k is extension without dot
        result[k.lower()] = v
    return result

def parse_remap(s):
    # format: "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header"
    # s is like "\"-*- C++ -*-\":\"C Header\""
    # Could be multiple separated by comma? Probably single.
    res=[]
    if not s:
        return res
    # Use similar split, but pattern is "search":"lang"
    # We'll parse using regex for "([^"]+)":\s*"([^"]+)" or '...':'...'
    # Also unquoted maybe
    # Simple: split by comma outside quotes
    parts=[]
    cur=""
    in_quote=False
    quote_char=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_quote:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==quote_char:
                in_quote=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_quote=True
                quote_char=ch
                cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                # But comma inside remap? Probably not
                parts.append(cur.strip())
                cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        # Find colon separating
        # Need to handle quoted colon
        # Find first colon not inside quotes
        in_q=False
        qc=None
        sep=-1
        for i,ch in enumerate(p):
            if in_q:
                if ch==qc:
                    in_q=False
            else:
                if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                    in_q=True
                    qc=ch
                elif ch==":":
                    sep=i
                    break
        if sep==-1:
            continue
        k=p[:sep].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        v=p[sep+1:].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        res.append((k,v))
    return res

# COCOMO calculation
def cocomo(code_lines, avg_wage=56286, overhead=2.4, eaf=1.0, project_type="organic"):
    # code_lines is total code lines (CLoC) ? scc uses Code lines sum for COCOMO, not Lines?
    # Check earlier: code lines 14 gave estimated cost 305, while code 14? Actually total code 14 in test_scc. 14 code lines produced 305 cost. So yes code lines used.
    # Use KSLOC = code /1000
    ksloc = code_lines / 1000.0
    if project_type.startswith("custom"):
        # parse custom,1,1,1,1  -> a,b,c,d
        try:
            parts=project_type.split(",")
            if len(parts)==5:
                a=float(parts[1]); b=float(parts[2]); c=float(parts[3]); d=float(parts[4])
            else:
                # fallback
                a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        except:
            a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label = project_type
    elif project_type == "organic":
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label="organic"
    elif project_type == "semi-detached":
        a,b,c,d=3.0,1.12,2.5,0.35
        project_label="semi-detached"
    elif project_type == "embedded":
        a,b,c,d=3.6,1.20,2.5,0.32
        project_label="embedded"
    else:
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label=project_type

    if ksloc == 0:
        effort=0.0
        schedule=0.0
        people=0.0
        cost=0.0
    else:
        effort = a * (ksloc ** b) * eaf  # person-months
        schedule = c * (effort ** d)
        people = effort / schedule if schedule !=0 else 0
        cost = effort * (avg_wage/12.0) * overhead
    return cost, schedule, people, project_label

# Directory walking
def load_ignore_patterns(dirpath, filename):
    path=os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
    patterns=[]
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            with open(path, errors='ignore') as f:
                for line in f:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line=="" or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    patterns.append(line)
        except:
            pass
    return patterns

def matches_ignore(path, patterns, is_dir=False):
    # Simplified: fnmatch
    # patterns like .gitignore syntax: support * , ? etc.
    # We'll use fnmatch.fnmatch basename and also full relative?
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    for pat in patterns:
        # handle negation ! not needed
        if pat.startswith("!"):
            continue
        # handle directory slash
        if pat.endswith("/"):
            pat=pat.rstrip("/")
            if os.path.isdir(path) and fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat):
                return True
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat+"/*"):
                return True
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat):
            return True
        # also check fnmatch with path
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(path, "*/"+pat):
            return True
    return False

def walk_files(start_paths, exclude_dirs, exclude_files, exclude_ext, include_ext, not_match_regexes, include_symlinks, no_gitignore, no_ignore, no_scc_ignore, count_ignore):
    collected=[]
    # Build regex list
    regexes=[]
    for pat in not_match_regexes:
        try:
            regexes.append(re.compile(pat))
        except:
            pass
    # For each start path
    for start in start_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(start):
            # scc prints to stdout "file or directory could not be read: ..."
            # We'll handle outside
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(start) or os.path.islink(start):
            # Single file handling: if it's symlink and include_symlinks false, skip?
            if os.path.islink(start) and not include_symlinks:
                # scc skips symlink files unless include_symlinks
                # But if file is passed explicitly, does it count? Original tested symlink link.py in /tmp/c counted via dir but not via file? The test with symlink file /tmp/c/link.py direct? We had link vs include: symlink file not counted unless include-symlinks.
                # For single file path that is symlink, if not include_symlinks, skip
                continue
            # Check not_match
            skip=False
            for rx in regexes:
                if rx.search(start):
                    skip=True
                    break
            if skip:
                continue
            # Check exclude_file
            if os.path.basename(start) in exclude_files:
                continue
            # Check exclude_ext/include_ext
            _, ext = os.path.splitext(start)
            ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
            if include_ext is not None:
                if ext not in include_ext:
                    continue
            if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext:
                continue
            # Not checking ignore files for single file? Maybe not
            collected.append(start)
        else:
            # Directory walk
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(start, topdown=True, followlinks=include_symlinks):
                # Exclude dirs
                # Modify dirs in-place
                dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in exclude_dirs]
                # also filter by not_match regex for dirs
                new_dirs=[]
                for d in dirs:
                    full=os.path.join(root,d)
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(full) or rx.search(d):
                            skip=True
                            break
                    if not skip:
                        new_dirs.append(d)
                dirs[:]=new_dirs

                # Load ignore patterns for this dir if not count_ignore
                ignore_patterns=[]
                scc_ignore_patterns=[]
                gitignore_patterns=[]
                gitmodules_patterns=[]

                if not count_ignore and not no_ignore:
                    ignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".ignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_scc_ignore:
                    scc_ignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".sccignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_gitignore:
                    gitignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".gitignore")
                # .gitmodules logic ignored for now

                # Combine patterns
                combined_ignore = ignore_patterns + scc_ignore_patterns + gitignore_patterns

                # Filter files
                for fname in files:
                    fpath=os.path.join(root, fname)
                    # symlink handling
                    if os.path.islink(fpath) and not include_symlinks:
                        continue
                    # not_match
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(fpath) or rx.search(fname):
                            skip=True
                            break
                    if skip:
                        continue
                    if fname in exclude_files:
                        continue
                    # ignore patterns check (using relative? simplified)
                    if combined_ignore and matches_ignore(fpath, combined_ignore):
                        continue
                    if combined_ignore and matches_ignore(fname, combined_ignore):
                        continue
                    # also check if any ignore pattern matches dir components?
                    # Simplified: check basename
                    # ext filtering
                    _, ext = os.path.splitext(fname)
                    ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
                    if include_ext is not None:
                        if ext not in include_ext:
                            continue
                    if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext:
                        continue
                    collected.append(fpath)
    return collected

    # To more closely match observed, we'll use threshold: if b'\x00' in data[:8000] then binary if count >1 or not at end?

# Minified / generated detection
def is_minified(bytes_len, lines, threshold=255):
    if lines == 0:
        return False
    avg = bytes_len / lines
    return avg > threshold

def is_generated(content, markers=None):
    if markers is None:
        markers = ["do not edit","<auto-generated />"]
    # Check first 1024 bytes head for markers case-insensitive
    head = content[:2048].decode(errors='ignore').lower()
    for m in markers:
        if m.lower() in head:
            return True
    return False

# Helper to parse count-as string
def parse_count_as(s):
    # format: "jsp:htm,chead:\"C Header\" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header"
    # s is like "jsp:htm" or "jsp:htm,chead:\"C Header\""
    # Need to handle quotes
    result={}
    if not s:
        return result
    # Use csv-like split respecting quotes? Simplify split by comma not inside quotes
    parts=[]
    cur=""
    in_quote=False
    quote_char=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_quote:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==quote_char:
                in_quote=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_quote=True
                quote_char=ch
                cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip())
                cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        if ":" not in p:
            continue
        k,v = p.split(":",1)
        k=k.strip()
        v=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        # k is extension without dot
        result[k.lower()] = v
    return result

def parse_remap(s):
    # format: "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header"
    # s is like "\"-*- C++ -*-\":\"C Header\""
    # Could be multiple separated by comma? Probably single.
    res=[]
    if not s:
        return res
    # Use similar split, but pattern is "search":"lang"
    # We'll parse using regex for "([^"]+)":\s*"([^"]+)" or '...':'...'
    # Also unquoted maybe
    # Simple: split by comma outside quotes
    parts=[]
    cur=""
    in_quote=False
    quote_char=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_quote:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==quote_char:
                in_quote=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_quote=True
                quote_char=ch
                cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                # But comma inside remap? Probably not
                parts.append(cur.strip())
                cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        # Find colon separating
        # Need to handle quoted colon
        # Find first colon not inside quotes
        in_q=False
        qc=None
        sep=-1
        for i,ch in enumerate(p):
            if in_q:
                if ch==qc:
                    in_q=False
            else:
                if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                    in_q=True
                    qc=ch
                elif ch==":":
                    sep=i
                    break
        if sep==-1:

        k=p[:sep].strip().strip('"').strip("'")

# COCOMO calculation
def cocomo(code_lines, avg_wage=56286, overhead=2.4, eaf=1.0, project_type="organic"):
    # code_lines is total code lines (CLoC) ? scc uses Code lines sum for COCOMO, not Lines?
    # Check earlier: code lines 14 gave estimated cost 305, while code 14? Actually total code 14 in test_scc. 14 code lines produced 305 cost. So yes code lines used.
    # Use KSLOC = code /1000
    ksloc = code_lines / 1000.0
    if project_type.startswith("custom"):
        # parse custom,1,1,1,1  -> a,b,c,d
        try:
            parts=project_type.split(",")
            if len(parts)==5:
                a=float(parts[1]); b=float(parts[2]); c=float(parts[3]); d=float(parts[4])
            else:
                # fallback
                a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        except:
            a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label = project_type
    elif project_type == "organic":
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label="organic"
    elif project_type == "semi-detached":
        a,b,c,d=3.0,1.12,2.5,0.35
        project_label="semi-detached"
    elif project_type == "embedded":
        a,b,c,d=3.6,1.20,2.5,0.32
        project_label="embedded"
    else:
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        project_label=project_type

    if ksloc == 0:
        effort=0.0
        schedule=0.0
        people=0.0
        cost=0.0
    else:
        effort = a * (ksloc ** b) * eaf  # person-months
        schedule = c * (effort ** d)
        people = effort / schedule if schedule !=0 else 0
        cost = effort * (avg_wage/12.0) * overhead
    return cost, schedule, people, project_label

# Directory walking
def load_ignore_patterns(dirpath, filename):
    path=os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
    patterns=[]
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            with open(path, errors='ignore') as f:
                for line in f:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line=="" or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    patterns.append(line)
        except:
            pass
    return patterns

def matches_ignore(path, patterns, is_dir=False):
    # Simplified: fnmatch
    # patterns like .gitignore syntax: support * , ? etc.
    # We'll use fnmatch.fnmatch basename and also full relative?
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    for pat in patterns:
        # handle negation ! not needed
        if pat.startswith("!"):
            continue
        # handle directory slash
        if pat.endswith("/"):
            pat=pat.rstrip("/")
            if os.path.isdir(path) and fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat):
                return True
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat+"/*"):
                return True
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat):
            return True
        # also check fnmatch with path
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(path, "*/"+pat):
            return True
    return False

def walk_files(start_paths, exclude_dirs, exclude_files, exclude_ext, include_ext, not_match_regexes, include_symlinks, no_gitignore, no_ignore, no_scc_ignore, count_ignore):
    collected=[]
    # Build regex list
    regexes=[]
    for pat in not_match_regexes:
        try:
            regexes.append(re.compile(pat))
        except:
            pass
    # For each start path
    for start in start_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(start):
            # scc prints to stdout "file or directory could not be read: ..."
            # We'll handle outside
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(start) or os.path.islink(start):
            # Single file handling: if it's symlink and include_symlinks false, skip?
            if os.path.islink(start) and not include_symlinks:
                # scc skips symlink files unless include_symlinks
                # But if file is passed explicitly, does it count? Original tested symlink link.py in /tmp/c counted via dir but not via file? The test with symlink file /tmp/c/link.py direct? We had link vs include: symlink file not counted unless include-symlinks.
                # For single file path that is symlink, if not include_symlinks, skip
                continue
            # Check not_match
            skip=False
            for rx in regexes:
                if rx.search(start):
                    skip=True
                    break
            if skip:
                continue
            # Check exclude_file
            if os.path.basename(start) in exclude_files:
                continue
            # Check exclude_ext/include_ext
            _, ext = os.path.splitext(start)
            ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
            if include_ext is not None:
                if ext not in include_ext:
                    continue
            if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext:
                continue
            # Not checking ignore files for single file? Maybe not
            collected.append(start)
        else:
            # Directory walk
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(start, topdown=True, followlinks=include_symlinks):
                # Exclude dirs
                # Modify dirs in-place
                dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in exclude_dirs]
                # also filter by not_match regex for dirs
                new_dirs=[]
                for d in dirs:
                    full=os.path.join(root,d)
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(full) or rx.search(d):
                            skip=True
                            break
                    if not skip:
                        new_dirs.append(d)
                dirs[:]=new_dirs

                # Load ignore patterns for this dir if not count_ignore
                ignore_patterns=[]
                scc_ignore_patterns=[]
                gitignore_patterns=[]
                gitmodules_patterns=[]

                if not count_ignore and not no_ignore:
                    ignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".ignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_scc_ignore:
                    scc_ignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".sccignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_gitignore:
                    gitignore_patterns = load_ignore_patterns(root, ".gitignore")
                # .gitmodules logic ignored for now

                # Combine patterns
                combined_ignore = ignore_patterns + scc_ignore_patterns + gitignore_patterns

                # Filter files
                for fname in files:
                    fpath=os.path.join(root, fname)
                    # symlink handling
                    if os.path.islink(fpath) and not include_symlinks:
                        continue
                    # not_match
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(fpath) or rx.search(fname):
                            skip=True
                            break
                    if skip:
                        continue
                    if fname in exclude_files:
                        continue
                    # ignore patterns check (using relative? simplified)
                    if combined_ignore and matches_ignore(fpath, combined_ignore):
                        continue
                    if combined_ignore and matches_ignore(fname, combined_ignore):
                        continue
                    # also check if any ignore pattern matches dir components?
                    # Simplified: check basename
                    # ext filtering
                    _, ext = os.path.splitext(fname)
                    ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
                    if include_ext is not None:
                        if ext not in include_ext:
                            continue
                    if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext:
                        continue
                    collected.append(fpath)
    return collected

    # They also have other units; we just handle si/binary/mixed etc as same? But tests show they print unit in parentheses as (SI) or (BINARY) or (MIXED) matching argument upper.
    # We'll map

        "xkcd-kb": ("XKCD-KB", 1000),

        if in_block:
            comment+=1
            if block_end and block_end in raw_line:
                in_block=False
                block_end=None
            continue
        # line comment
        found=False
        for lc in line_comments:
            if stripped.startswith(lc):
                comment+=1
                found=True
                break
            if lc.upper()=="REM" and stripped.upper().startswith("REM"):
                comment+=1
                found=True
                break
        if found:
            continue
        if lang_name=="Python":
            if stripped.startswith('"""') or stripped.startswith("'''"):
                delim=stripped[:3]
                # count occurrences
                cnt=raw_line.count(delim)
                if cnt>=2:
                    comment+=1
                else:
                    comment+=1
                    in_block=True
                    block_end=delim
                continue
            code+=1
            continue
        block_found=False
        for bs,be in blocks:
            if bs in raw_line:
                start_idx=raw_line.find(bs)
                end_idx=raw_line.find(be, start_idx+len(bs))
                if end_idx!=-1:
                    before=raw_line[:start_idx].strip()
                    after=raw_line[end_idx+len(be):].strip()
                    if before=="" and after=="":
                        comment+=1
                    else:
                        code+=1
                    block_found=True
                    break
                else:
                    before=raw_line[:start_idx].strip()
                    if before=="":
                        comment+=1
                    else:
                        code+=1
                    in_block=True
                    block_end=be
                    block_found=True
                    break
        if block_found:
            continue
        code+=1
    complexity=0 if no_complexity else complexity_for_lang(lang_name, text)
    mean_line = (total_chars//total_lines) if total_lines else 0
    return {"Bytes":bytes_len,"Lines":total_lines,"Blank":blank,"Comment":comment,"Code":code,"Complexity":complexity,"MaxLine":max_line,"MeanLine":mean_line, "Text":text}

def detect_language(filepath, content_bytes=None, count_as_map=None, remap_unknown=None, remap_all=None):
    if count_as_map is None: count_as_map={}
    basename=os.path.basename(filepath)
    low_base=basename.lower()
    lang=None
    # compound check
    for ext, l in ext_to_lang.items():
        if "." in ext:
            if low_base.endswith(ext):
                lang=l
                break
    if lang is None:
        if low_base in filename_to_lang:
            lang=filename_to_lang[low_base]
        else:
            if "." in basename:
                ext=basename.rsplit(".",1)[1].lower()
                if ext in count_as_map:
                    dest=count_as_map[ext]
                    # dest could be language name or ext
                    found=None
                    for n,_ in language_list:
                        if n.lower()==dest.lower():
                            found=n
                            break
                    if found:
                        lang=found
                    else:
                        lang=ext_to_lang.get(dest.lower(), dest)
                elif ext in ext_to_lang:
                    lang=ext_to_lang[ext]
    # count_as already handled for ext case, but also for filename without ext? Already.
    # handle count_as for case where lang from filename but count_as maps extension? Not needed.
    # shebang
    if lang is None:
        try:
            head=content_bytes[:1024] if content_bytes else open(filepath,'rb').read(1024)
            if head.startswith(b'#!'):
                first_line=head.split(b'\n',1)[0].decode(errors='ignore').lower()
                if "python" in first_line:
                    lang="Python"
                elif "bash" in first_line or "sh" in first_line:
                    lang="Shell"
                elif "ruby" in first_line:
                    lang="Ruby"
                elif "perl" in first_line:
                    lang="Perl"
                elif "node" in first_line:
                    lang="JavaScript"
        except:
            pass
    if lang is None and remap_unknown:
        try:
            txt=(content_bytes[:4096].decode(errors='ignore') if content_bytes else open(filepath,'rb').read(4096).decode(errors='ignore'))
        except:
            txt=""
        for pat,dest in remap_unknown:
            if pat in txt:
                dest=dest.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                found=None
                for n,_ in language_list:
                    if n.lower()==dest.lower():
                        found=n
                        break
                if found: lang=found
                else: lang=ext_to_lang.get(dest.lower(), dest)
                break
    elif remap_all:
        try:
            txt=(content_bytes[:4096].decode(errors='ignore') if content_bytes else open(filepath,'rb').read(4096).decode(errors='ignore'))
        except:
            txt=""
        for pat,dest in remap_all:
            if pat in txt:
                dest=dest.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                found=None
                for n,_ in language_list:
                    if n.lower()==dest.lower():
                        found=n
                        break
                if found: lang=found
                else: lang=ext_to_lang.get(dest.lower(), dest)
                break
    return lang

def parse_count_as(s):
    result={}
    if not s: return result
    parts=[]
    cur=""; in_q=False; qc=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_q:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==qc: in_q=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_q=True; qc=ch; cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip(): parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        if ":" not in p: continue
        k,v=p.split(":",1)
        result[k.strip().lower()]=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return result

def parse_remap(s):
    res=[]
    if not s: return res
    parts=[]
    cur=""; in_q=False; qc=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_q:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==qc: in_q=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_q=True; qc=ch; cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip(): parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        in_q=False; qc=None; sep=-1
        for i,ch in enumerate(p):
            if in_q:
                if ch==qc: in_q=False
            else:
                if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                    in_q=True; qc=ch
                elif ch==":":
                    sep=i; break
        if sep==-1: continue
        k=p[:sep].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        v=p[sep+1:].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        res.append((k,v))
    return res

def cocomo(code_lines, avg_wage=56286, overhead=2.4, eaf=1.0, project_type="organic"):
    ksloc=code_lines/1000.0
    if project_type.startswith("custom"):
        try:
            parts=project_type.split(",")
            a=float(parts[1]); b=float(parts[2]); c=float(parts[3]); d=float(parts[4])
        except:
            a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        label=project_type
    elif project_type=="organic":
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38; label="organic"
    elif project_type=="semi-detached":
        a,b,c,d=3.0,1.12,2.5,0.35; label="semi-detached"
    elif project_type=="embedded":
        a,b,c,d=3.6,1.20,2.5,0.32; label="embedded"
    else:
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38; label=project_type
    if ksloc==0:
        return 0,0,0,label
    effort=a*(ksloc**b)*eaf
    schedule=c*(effort**d)
    people=effort/schedule if schedule else 0
    cost=effort*(avg_wage/12)*overhead
    return cost,schedule,people,label

def locomo_estimate(total_code, total_complexity, preset="medium", config=None, cycles_override=None, input_price=None, output_price=None, tps_override=None, review_minutes=None):
    presets={"large":{"input_price":5,"output_price":15,"tps":30},"medium":{"input_price":3,"output_price":15,"tps":50},"small":{"input_price":0.5,"output_price":2,"tps":100},"local":{"input_price":0,"output_price":0,"tps":15}}
    prices=presets.get(preset, presets["medium"]).copy()
    if input_price is not None: prices["input_price"]=input_price
    if output_price is not None: prices["output_price"]=output_price
    tps=prices["tps"]
    if tps_override is not None: tps=tps_override
    if config:
        try:
            parts=config.split(",")
            tpls=float(parts[0]); ipls=float(parts[1]); cw=float(parts[2]); its=float(parts[3]); iw=float(parts[4])
        except:
            tpls,ipls,cw,its,iw=15,30,10,1.5,1
    else:
        tpls,ipls,cw,its,iw=15,30,10,1.5,1
    if cycles_override is not None:
        cycles=cycles_override
    else:
        if total_code==0:
            cycles=its
        else:
            ratio=total_complexity/total_code if total_code else 0
            cycles=its + iw*math.sqrt(ratio)*2
    if total_code==0:
        avg_mult=its
    else:
        ratio=total_complexity/total_code if total_code else 0
        avg_mult=its + cw*(ratio**0.7)
    base_input=total_code*ipls
    base_output=total_code*tpls
    input_tokens=base_input*avg_mult*(2/3) if total_code else 0
    output_tokens=base_output*avg_mult*0.25 if total_code else 0
    gen_seconds=output_tokens/tps if tps else 0
    if review_minutes is None: review_minutes=0.01
    review_hours=total_code*review_minutes/60.0
    cost=input_tokens*prices["input_price"]/1e6 + output_tokens*prices["output_price"]/1e6
    return {"input_tokens":input_tokens,"output_tokens":output_tokens,"cycles":cycles,"avg_mult":avg_mult,"gen_seconds":gen_seconds,"review_hours":review_hours,"cost":cost,"preset":preset,"tps":tps}

def load_ignore_patterns(dirpath, filename):
    path=os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
    patterns=[]
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            with open(path, errors='ignore') as f:
                for line in f:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line=="" or line.startswith("#"): continue
                    patterns.append(line)
        except:
            pass
    return patterns

def matches_ignore(path, patterns):
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    for pat in patterns:
        if pat.startswith("!"): continue
        if pat.endswith("/"): pat=pat.rstrip("/")
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, "*/"+pat):
            return True
    return False

def walk_files(start_paths, exclude_dirs, exclude_files, exclude_ext, include_ext, not_match_regexes, include_symlinks, no_gitignore, no_ignore, no_scc_ignore, count_ignore):
    collected=[]
    regexes=[]
    for pat in not_match_regexes:
        try: regexes.append(re.compile(pat))
        except: pass
    for start in start_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(start):
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(start) or os.path.islink(start):
            if os.path.islink(start) and not include_symlinks:
                continue
            skip=False
            for rx in regexes:
                if rx.search(start): skip=True; break
            if skip: continue
            if os.path.basename(start) in exclude_files: continue
            _, ext=os.path.splitext(start); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
            if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
            if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
            collected.append(start)
        else:
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(start, topdown=True, followlinks=include_symlinks):
                dirs[:]=[d for d in dirs if d not in exclude_dirs]
                nd=[]
                for d in dirs:
                    full=os.path.join(root,d)
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(full) or rx.search(d): skip=True; break
                    if not skip: nd.append(d)
                dirs[:]=nd
                combined=[]
                if not count_ignore and not no_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".ignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_scc_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".sccignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_gitignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".gitignore")
                for fname in files:
                    fpath=os.path.join(root,fname)
                    if os.path.islink(fpath) and not include_symlinks: continue
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(fpath) or rx.search(fname): skip=True; break
                    if skip: continue
                    if fname in exclude_files: continue
                    if combined and (matches_ignore(fpath, combined) or matches_ignore(fname, combined)):
                        continue
                    _, ext=os.path.splitext(fname); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
                    if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
                    if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
                    collected.append(fpath)
    return collected

def format_size(bytes_len, unit="si"):
    units={"si":("SI",1000),"binary":("BINARY",1024),"mixed":("MIXED",1000),"xkcd-kb":("XKCD-KB",1000),"xkcd-kelly":("XKCD-KELLY",1000),"xkcd-imaginary":("XKCD-IMAGINARY",1000),"xkcd-intel":("XKCD-INTEL",1000),"xkcd-drive":("XKCD-DRIVE",1000),"xkcd-bakers":("XKCD-BAKERS",1000)}
    label, base=units.get(unit.lower(), ("SI",1000))
    if base==1024:
        mb=bytes_len/(1024*1024)
    else:
        mb=bytes_len/1e6
    return f"{bytes_len} bytes, {mb:.3f} megabytes ({label})"

def parse_count_as(s):
    result={}
    if not s: return result
    parts=[]
    cur=""; in_q=False; qc=None
    for ch in s:

            cur+=ch
            if ch==qc: in_q=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:

            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip(): parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        if ":" not in p: continue

def parse_remap(s):
    res=[]
    if not s: return res
    parts=[]
    cur=""; in_q=False; qc=None
    for ch in s:
        if in_q:
            cur+=ch
            if ch==qc: in_q=False
        else:
            if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                in_q=True; qc=ch; cur+=ch
            elif ch==",":
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur=""
            else:
                cur+=ch
    if cur.strip(): parts.append(cur.strip())
    for p in parts:
        in_q=False; qc=None; sep=-1
        for i,ch in enumerate(p):
            if in_q:
                if ch==qc: in_q=False
            else:
                if ch in ['"',"'"]:
                    in_q=True; qc=ch
                elif ch==":":
                    sep=i; break
        if sep==-1: continue
        k=p[:sep].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        v=p[sep+1:].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        res.append((k,v))
    return res

def cocomo(code_lines, avg_wage=56286, overhead=2.4, eaf=1.0, project_type="organic"):
    ksloc=code_lines/1000.0
    if project_type.startswith("custom"):
        try:
            parts=project_type.split(",")
            a=float(parts[1]); b=float(parts[2]); c=float(parts[3]); d=float(parts[4])
        except:
            a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38
        label=project_type
    elif project_type=="organic":
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38; label="organic"
    elif project_type=="semi-detached":
        a,b,c,d=3.0,1.12,2.5,0.35; label="semi-detached"
    elif project_type=="embedded":
        a,b,c,d=3.6,1.20,2.5,0.32; label="embedded"
    else:
        a,b,c,d=2.4,1.05,2.5,0.38; label=project_type
    if ksloc==0:
        return 0,0,0,label
    effort=a*(ksloc**b)*eaf
    schedule=c*(effort**d)
    people=effort/schedule if schedule else 0
    cost=effort*(avg_wage/12)*overhead
    return cost,schedule,people,label

def locomo_estimate(total_code, total_complexity, preset="medium", config=None, cycles_override=None, input_price=None, output_price=None, tps_override=None, review_minutes=None):
    presets={"large":{"input_price":5,"output_price":15,"tps":30},"medium":{"input_price":3,"output_price":15,"tps":50},"small":{"input_price":0.5,"output_price":2,"tps":100},"local":{"input_price":0,"output_price":0,"tps":15}}
    prices=presets.get(preset, presets["medium"]).copy()

    if output_price is not None: prices["output_price"]=output_price

            parts=config.split(",")

        tpls,ipls,cw,its,iw=15,30,10,1.5,1

        cycles=cycles_override

    output_tokens=base_output*avg_mult*0.25 if total_code else 0

    if review_minutes is None: review_minutes=0.01

def load_ignore_patterns(dirpath, filename):
    path=os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
    patterns=[]
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            with open(path, errors='ignore') as f:
                for line in f:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line=="" or line.startswith("#"): continue
                    patterns.append(line)
        except:
            pass
    return patterns

def matches_ignore(path, patterns):
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    for pat in patterns:
        if pat.startswith("!"): continue
        if pat.endswith("/"): pat=pat.rstrip("/")
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, "*/"+pat):
            return True
    return False

def walk_files(start_paths, exclude_dirs, exclude_files, exclude_ext, include_ext, not_match_regexes, include_symlinks, no_gitignore, no_ignore, no_scc_ignore, count_ignore):
    collected=[]
    regexes=[]
    for pat in not_match_regexes:
        try: regexes.append(re.compile(pat))
        except: pass
    for start in start_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(start):
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(start) or os.path.islink(start):
            if os.path.islink(start) and not include_symlinks:
                continue
            skip=False
            for rx in regexes:
                if rx.search(start): skip=True; break
            if skip: continue
            if os.path.basename(start) in exclude_files: continue
            _, ext=os.path.splitext(start); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
            if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
            if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
            collected.append(start)
        else:
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(start, topdown=True, followlinks=include_symlinks):
                dirs[:]=[d for d in dirs if d not in exclude_dirs]
                nd=[]
                for d in dirs:
                    full=os.path.join(root,d)
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(full) or rx.search(d): skip=True; break
                    if not skip: nd.append(d)
                dirs[:]=nd
                combined=[]
                if not count_ignore and not no_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".ignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_scc_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".sccignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_gitignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".gitignore")
                for fname in files:
                    fpath=os.path.join(root,fname)
                    if os.path.islink(fpath) and not include_symlinks: continue
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(fpath) or rx.search(fname): skip=True; break
                    if skip: continue
                    if fname in exclude_files: continue
                    if combined and (matches_ignore(fpath, combined) or matches_ignore(fname, combined)):
                        continue
                    _, ext=os.path.splitext(fname); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
                    if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
                    if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
                    collected.append(fpath)
    return collected

def format_size(bytes_len, unit="si"):
    units={"si":("SI",1000),"binary":("BINARY",1024),"mixed":("MIXED",1000),"xkcd-kb":("XKCD-KB",1000),"xkcd-kelly":("XKCD-KELLY",1000),"xkcd-imaginary":("XKCD-IMAGINARY",1000),"xkcd-intel":("XKCD-INTEL",1000),"xkcd-drive":("XKCD-DRIVE",1000),"xkcd-bakers":("XKCD-BAKERS",1000)}

        "--wide":("wide","bool"),
        "-w":("wide","bool"),
    }
    # For string flags that may have = syntax: --flag=value
    args=[]
    for a in argv:
        if "=" in a and a.startswith("-"):
            # split
            flag, val = a.split("=",1)
            args.append(flag)
            args.append(val)
        else:
            args.append(a)
    i=0
    positional=[]
    while i < len(args):
        a=args[i]
        if a=="--":
            positional.extend(args[i+1:])
            break
        if a.startswith("-"):
            # check if flag is known
            if a not in flag_specs:
                error_exit(f"Error: unknown flag: {a}")
            key, typ = flag_specs[a]
            if typ=="bool":
                opts[key]=True
                i+=1
            else:
                # need value
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    error_exit(f"Error: flag needs an argument: {a}")
                val=args[i+1]
                # Validate type for errors as cobra does
                if typ=="int":
                    try:
                        iv=int(val)
                    except:
                        error_exit(f'Error: invalid argument "{val}" for "{a}" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "{val}": invalid syntax')

                    try:

                        opts[key]=[x.strip() for x in val.split(",") if x.strip()!=""]
                elif typ=="stringArray":
                    # For --not-match, can be repeated, accumulate
                    if opts[key] is None:
                        opts[key]=[]
                    opts[key].append(val)
                i+=2
        else:
            positional.append(a)
            i+=1
    opts["_positional"]=positional
    # Handle implies

    if opts["no_gen"]:

        # implies complexity? but we handle
        pass
    if opts["min_gen"]:
        opts["min"]=True

    # sloccount-format implies? just flag
    return opts

def matches_ignore(path, patterns):
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    for pat in patterns:
        if pat.startswith("!"): continue
        if pat.endswith("/"): pat=pat.rstrip("/")
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, "*/"+pat):
            return True
    return False

def walk_files(start_paths, exclude_dirs, exclude_files, exclude_ext, include_ext, not_match_regexes, include_symlinks, no_gitignore, no_ignore, no_scc_ignore, count_ignore):
    collected=[]
    regexes=[]
    for pat in not_match_regexes:
        try: regexes.append(re.compile(pat))
        except: pass
    for start in start_paths:
        if not os.path.exists(start):
            continue
        if os.path.isfile(start) or os.path.islink(start):
            if os.path.islink(start) and not include_symlinks:
                continue
            skip=False
            for rx in regexes:
                if rx.search(start): skip=True; break
            if skip: continue
            if os.path.basename(start) in exclude_files: continue
            _, ext=os.path.splitext(start); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
            if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
            if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
            collected.append(start)
        else:
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(start, topdown=True, followlinks=include_symlinks):
                dirs[:]=[d for d in dirs if d not in exclude_dirs]
                nd=[]
                for d in dirs:
                    full=os.path.join(root,d)
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(full) or rx.search(d): skip=True; break
                    if not skip: nd.append(d)
                dirs[:]=nd
                combined=[]
                if not count_ignore and not no_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".ignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_scc_ignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".sccignore")
                if not count_ignore and not no_gitignore:
                    combined+=load_ignore_patterns(root, ".gitignore")
                for fname in files:
                    fpath=os.path.join(root,fname)
                    if os.path.islink(fpath) and not include_symlinks: continue
                    skip=False
                    for rx in regexes:
                        if rx.search(fpath) or rx.search(fname): skip=True; break
                    if skip: continue
                    if fname in exclude_files: continue
                    if combined and (matches_ignore(fpath, combined) or matches_ignore(fname, combined)):
                        continue
                    _, ext=os.path.splitext(fname); ext=ext.lstrip(".").lower()
                    if include_ext is not None and ext not in include_ext: continue
                    if exclude_ext and ext in exclude_ext: continue
                    collected.append(fpath)
    return collected
